title: A kit's dynamics-row planar shaping drives real movement, and authoring both response and dynamics refuses
binding: The positive leg boots a minimal fixture whose one kit shapes planar velocity through a dynamics row (f=2.5, zeta=1, r=0) instead of a response table, confirms world.kits echoes shaping=dynamics:stride, drives a body.fly forward segment, and asserts the settled pose after it fully plays out — proving the follower genuinely integrated real displacement, not merely validated. The fixture's motion program deliberately omits ApplyVerticalGravity and the read waits 220 ticks past the segment's 480-tick expiry, so the observed pose is a genuine fixed point: world.wait guarantees AT LEAST its tick count (a loaded host's catch-up burst can overshoot the release by up to 60 ticks before the console pump drains), and only a stationary pose survives that read-tick spread exactly. The discriminating leg re-authors the SAME kit live through world.row.set kits, this time carrying BOTH response and dynamics on the SAME motion row; the mutation is refused by the exactly-one-of-response-or-dynamics rule, and a follow-up world.kits shows the kit unchanged — proving the refused mutation never applied.

expect.name: both-response-and-dynamics-refused
expect.text: kits[0].motion authors both response and dynamics 'stride' - a kit shapes planar velocity through exactly one.
